A.explanation: The wavelength is about $0.40 \text{ m}$ and the fundamental in a closed-open tube is $L = \lambda/4 \approx 0.10 \text{ m} = 10 \text{ cm}$.

hints: Notice the tube is closed at one end and open at the other, so there must be a displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end.

First find the wavelength from $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $f = 820 \text{ Hz}$, then divide by 4 and convert to $\text{cm}$.
walkthrough: Identify the end conditions: closed end is a node and open end is an antinode for the stationary sound wave.
For the lowest possible frequency, the standing wave is the fundamental, so the tube length holds a quarter wave: $L = \lambda/4$.
Use $v = f\lambda$ to find $\lambda = v/f = 330/820 \text{ m} \approx 0.402 \text{ m}$.
Check units: $\lambda$ is in metres, about $40.2 \text{ cm}$.
Calculate the tube length: $L = \lambda/4 \approx 0.402/4 \text{ m} \approx 0.101 \text{ m} \approx 10 \text{ cm}$.
